own_solution.law: Newton's second law along the incline with kinetic friction: a = g(sin(theta) - mu_k cos(theta)); kinematics v^2 = 2 a d from rest
assumptions: Coulomb kinetic friction with constant mu_k = 0.1
rigid planar incline, block does not tip

notes: All claims agree with pass 1. a = 5.5486 m/s^2. Checked R answers: d+q = 6, 7, 8 m give sqrt(66.583) = 8.15985, sqrt(77.680) = 8.81364, sqrt(88.778) = 9.42218 m/s. Base 7.44889 m/s. Mass cancellation expression reduces to sqrt(2 d g (sin(theta) - mu cos(theta))), independent of q. K regime q < tan(theta) = 0.839 contains all listed values 0.25, 0.35, 0.45 (each also exceeds mu_k = 0.1, so physically consistent); reference expression 0 outside the regime (block stays at rest) is correct. Minimal pairs T1CCB/T6528 and T6FC4/T00F7 each state 2 m and differ only in where the earlier sliding happened. Units consistent.
